There's a short window after a Zoom call where you still remember everything clearly: what was decided, what you committed to, what needs to go in the CRM before you forget the details. Most of that window gets spent typing. If you're looking at ways to move faster through the post-meeting writing queue,[voice dictation for Zoom](https://willowvoice.com/) fits into the workflow you already have without changing a single thing about how your calls run.


**Willow Voice is a voice dictation tool built for the writing around Zoom meetings: it types what you say into any text field around the call, from Zoom Chat to Gmail, Slack, Notion, and Salesforce, on Mac, Windows, and iOS.** It does not record or transcribe the meeting itself. One hotkey (fn on Mac, Win + Left Shift on Windows) starts dictation in whatever field is focused, with ~200ms latency versus 700ms or more for many competing dictation tools, and 98%+ accuracy with 3x fewer errors than built-in tools.


**TLDR:**


-


Transcription records what was said; dictation handles the writing work that follows.


-


Speaking runs at 150 WPM versus 40 WPM typing, and a Stanford study of speech recognition found it about 3x faster than typing on a phone, so a 10-minute typing task takes closer to 3 minutes to speak.


-


Speak your notes within 5 to 15 minutes of hanging up, since forgetting-curve research shows roughly half of newly learned material fades within the first hour.


-


A system-wide hotkey activates dictation in any text field alongside Zoom, including Chat, Google Docs, Notion, Salesforce, and Slack.


-


The dictation tool covered below offers a free plan with unlimited AI dictation and no word cap, an individual plan with faster, more accurate dictation and unlimited AI drafting, and team plans with shared dictionaries and admin controls, with SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance across the board.


## Voice Dictation vs. Meeting Transcription: Two Different Problems


Meeting transcription and voice dictation solve opposite problems, and confusing them leads to picking the wrong tool.


Transcription tools, such as Zoom's built-in AI, Otter.ai, Grain, and Tactiq, listen passively to a call and convert what was said into a record: a transcript, a summary, maybe some action items pulled from the audio. Useful, but it stops there.


Voice dictation runs the other direction. It lets you speak to type anywhere on your screen, into any text field, at any time: chat messages, follow-up emails, shared docs, Slack threads. You talk, text appears. The writing work Zoom generates doesn't end when the call does, and that output comes from you, sitting down to write after the meeting ends.


## The Writing Work Zoom Meetings Create


A one-hour Zoom call rarely ends at the one-hour mark. What follows is a writing queue: follow-up emails, Slack summaries, CRM updates, action-item docs, and sprint notes, each one a separate typing task.


The stakes are higher than they feel. Harvard Business Review reports that executives spend an average of[nearly 23 hours a week](https://hbr.org/2017/07/stop-the-meeting-madness) in meetings, and a[replication of Ebbinghaus' forgetting curve](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4492928/) found roughly half of newly learned material fades within the first hour. That is bad news for[executives writing meeting follow-ups](https://willowvoice.com/blog/executives-write-meeting-follow-ups-faster-willow) who wait until the end of the day.


## How Voice Dictation Fits into a Zoom Workflow


Voice dictation fits into the writing surfaces you already use around Zoom, without touching the meeting audio or recording. Three moments where it pays off:


-


Before the call, speak a context brief, agenda, or talking points into a Notion or Google Doc instead of typing it out.


-


During the call, speak into Zoom Chat, a shared doc, or a notes app.


-


After the call, speak follow-up emails, Slack summaries, action-item lists, and CRM notes while details are still fresh.


## Using Voice Input in Zoom Chat and Shared Docs During a Meeting


The mechanics are simple: a system-wide hotkey activates dictation in whatever text field is active on your screen. Zoom has no awareness it's happening. You're just typing, except you're speaking.


That applies to any surface running alongside the call:


-


[Voice dictation in Zoom Chat](https://willowvoice.com/use-cases/zoom) : speak your comment and it lands in the thread


-


A shared Google Doc: speak edits or action items as decisions happen


-


[AI voice dictation in Notion](https://willowvoice.com/blog/how-to-use-ai-voice-dictation-in-notion) or Confluence: log notes without leaving the call


-


Any personal notes app: capture anything without touching the keyboard


When a decision gets made mid-call, you can document it in the moment instead of reconstructing it from memory later. A system-level dictation tool works below the application layer, with no plugins and no per-app setup required.


## Clearing the Post-Meeting Writing Queue With Voice


The queue that forms when you hang up is time-sensitive: follow-up email, Slack summary, CRM update, sprint notes, recap doc. Speak your notes within 5 to 15 minutes of hanging up, while context is still intact. Wait longer and the details fade.


A rough working order for clearing the queue by voice:


-


[Voice dictation in Gmail](https://willowvoice.com/blog/ai-voice-dictation-gmail) or Outlook: speak the summary, next steps, and commitments made.


-


[AI voice dictation in Slack](https://willowvoice.com/blog/how-to-use-ai-voice-dictation-slack) for the team: one spoken paragraph captures decisions and assigns action items, no second meeting needed.


-


CRM update in Salesforce or HubSpot: click into the notes field and speak the deal update, no reformatting required.


-


Sprint notes in Linear or Jira: speak ticket updates and priority changes while technical details are still precise.


-


Recap doc in Notion or Confluence: speak a structured summary covering decisions, open questions, and next steps in one pass.


## Voice Dictation vs. Zoom's Built-In AI Features


Zoom's AI Companion does real work: a[meeting summary with AI](https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0058013) and next steps after the call, plus AI-drafted messages inside Zoom Team Chat and Zoom Mail. Otter.ai covers similar ground across Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams with searchable transcripts, recaps, and AI-drafted follow-up emails.


Both tools generate content from the meeting audio, and Otter can push AI notes into Salesforce or HubSpot, but neither types what you say into Gmail, Linear, Slack, or any field you click into. Built-in dictation in macOS and Windows does reach any field, but limited vocabulary learning means names and client terms often need manual fixes.

## Microphone Setup for Using Voice Dictation on Video Calls


Mic sharing between Zoom and a dictation tool normally works fine: most operating systems let multiple apps read the same input stream at once, so the two run in parallel. Conflicts are rare and usually limited to older drivers or locked corporate audio devices.


Audio bleed is the bigger concern. Microphone quality alone can swing dictation accuracy by roughly 10 to 15 percent, and call audio leaking from speakers into the mic makes it worse, so microphone choice matters more here than in quiet solo dictation.


-


Wireless earbuds with built-in mics (AirPods Pro or equivalent) keep the mic close to your mouth and cut room noise on calls.


-


USB close-talk headsets (Jabra Evolve, Logitech H390) sit 1 to 2 inches from your mouth and reject ambient noise well for frequent voice input.


-


Desktop USB condensers (Blue Yeti, Rode NT-USB) pick up more room sound, so wear headphones to prevent speaker bleed into the mic.


Built-in laptop mics are the weakest option, picking up keyboard sounds, room echo, and call audio from speakers at once.

## FAQs


### Can I use voice dictation for Zoom meetings without installing any plugins?


Yes. Willow Voice activates with a hotkey (fn on Mac, Win + Left Shift on Windows) inside any text field, with no plugins or per-app setup. Zoom has no awareness it is running, so you click into a chat box, doc, or notes app and speak.


### What's the best way to clear post-meeting follow-ups faster after a Zoom call?


Speak right after hanging up, while context is intact. Open Gmail or Slack, press the hotkey, and dictate the follow-up: a message that takes ten minutes to type takes under three to speak at 150 WPM versus 40 WPM typing. Clearing the full queue within five to fifteen minutes beats reconstructing it from memory later.


### How do I prevent Zoom audio from degrading my dictation accuracy?


Microphone choice matters most. Wireless earbuds (AirPods Pro or equivalent) or a USB close-talk headset like a Jabra Evolve keep the mic near your mouth and cut room noise. Avoid desktop speakers, since call audio bleeding into the mic hurts accuracy, and microphone quality alone can shift accuracy by ten to fifteen percent.


### Willow Voice vs. Zoom AI Companion: what does each one actually handle?


Zoom AI Companion works from Zoom audio and produces a transcript, summary, and action items. Willow Voice handles what comes after: the follow-up email, the CRM field, and the Slack summary. Zoom AI gives you a record of what was said; voice dictation gets it into the right place faster than typing.
